claims.title: Frankl union-closed sets conjecture
claims.statement: Every finite union-closed family of sets (other than the trivial family) contains an element present in at least half the members. Verified computationally for families up to moderate size, no general proof known.

axis_texts.semantic: In any union-closed family some element must be abundant; abundance is forced by closure alone.
axis_texts.mechanism: closure operation forces concentration of element frequencies
axis_texts.math_structure: set families closure operators frequency counting extremal combinatorics
axis_texts.problem_shape: local rule to global counting guarantee existence of abundant object
axis_texts.failure: proof attempts reduce to frequency vectors without exploitable structure

claims.title: Glass transition: thermodynamic transition or kinetic crossover?
claims.statement: Whether the structural glass transition reflects a genuine underlying thermodynamic phase transition (e.g., an ideal random first-order transition) or is merely a smooth kinetic slowdown remains unresolved.

axis_texts.semantic: Distinguish a genuine collective transition from a smooth finite-time crossover in supercooled liquids.
axis_texts.mechanism: separate thermodynamic singularity from dynamical arrest mechanisms
axis_texts.math_structure: energy landscapes metastability mode-coupling random first order transition
axis_texts.problem_shape: genuine singularity versus finite-size finite-time artifact
axis_texts.failure: every proposed static signature has a kinetic control that mimics it

claims.title: Planted clique: average-case hardness beyond log n
claims.statement: Recovering a planted clique of size k in G(n,1/2) is easy when k exceeds ~sqrt(n) spectral thresholds and conjectured hard near log(n); proving average-case hardness for k between log n and sqrt n, or even ruling out polynomial algorithms below sqrt(n)/log^2(n) for natural semidefinite hierarchies, is open.

axis_texts.semantic: Locate the true computational threshold for detecting a planted structure inside a random graph.
axis_texts.mechanism: separate information-theoretic possibility from algorithmic reachability
axis_texts.math_structure: random graphs spectral methods semidefinite programming sum-of-squares lower bounds
axis_texts.problem_shape: threshold location; proving absence of algorithms rather than presence
axis_texts.failure: lower bounds restricted to narrow algorithm classes; reductions circular

claims.title: Edit distance quadratic time barrier
claims.statement: Whether edit distance on strings admits a strongly subquadratic algorithm is equivalent to the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis being false; decades of attempts produced only log-factor improvements and conditional barrier results.

axis_texts.semantic: Prove or break the quadratic-time barrier for sequence comparison.
axis_texts.mechanism: conditional lower bound via fine-grained reductions; search for exploitable string structure
axis_texts.math_structure: dynamic programming fine-grained complexity SETH reductions orthogonal vectors
axis_texts.problem_shape: prove impossibility or find hidden structure enabling speedup
axis_texts.failure: all known techniques hit the alignment-table quadratic information content

claims.title: Intermittency anomalies in turbulence
claims.statement: Velocity-gradient statistics in high-Reynolds turbulence show anomalous scaling exponents not explained by Kolmogorov 1941 theory; no derivation of the multifractal spectrum from the Navier-Stokes equations exists.

axis_texts.semantic: Derive anomalous scaling of extreme fluctuations from the governing dynamics instead of fitting it.
axis_texts.mechanism: extreme events dominate moments; cascade models parameterize rather than derive
axis_texts.math_structure: multifractal formalism structure functions scale invariance breakdown large deviations
axis_texts.problem_shape: fitting phenomenology replaced by first-principles derivation
axis_texts.failure: cascade models are descriptive; closures miss intermittency universally

claims.title: Physical origin of enzyme catalytic power
claims.statement: Enzymes accelerate reactions by up to 10^20-fold, but how much comes from transition-state stabilization, ground-state destabilization, dynamical effects, and preorganization remains contested; no predictive theory computes rate acceleration from structure alone.

axis_texts.semantic: Decompose catalytic power into physically separable contributions with predictive power.
axis_texts.mechanism: rate acceleration decomposed into candidate contributions that resist clean separation
axis_texts.math_structure: transition state theory free energy surfaces reorganization protein dynamics
axis_texts.failure: each decomposition depends on arbitrary partitioning of the free energy surface

claims.title: Maintenance of sex and recombination
claims.statement: Sex carries the twofold cost of males and breaks up successful gene combinations, yet recombination dominates eukaryotic reproduction. Which advantage reliably overcomes these costs in nature remains unsettled among many proposed mechanisms.

axis_texts.semantic: Identify the advantage that systematically pays the twofold cost of sexual reproduction.
axis_texts.mechanism: recombination reshuffles variation; candidate benefits are condition-dependent
axis_texts.math_structure: population genetics linkage disequilibrium selection epistasis mutation load
axis_texts.failure: every proposed benefit works in some regime and fails in others; no universal winner demonstrated

claims.title: Mechanism of general anesthesia
claims.statement: How diverse agents (inert gases, halogenated ethers, barbiturates) reversibly abolish consciousness through shared circuit-level mechanisms remains unexplained despite identified molecular targets like GABA-A receptors.

axis_texts.semantic: Explain why chemically heterogeneous agents produce one reversible behavioral endpoint.
axis_texts.mechanism: diverse molecular targets converge on unknown circuit-level integration mechanism
axis_texts.math_structure: neural circuits excitation inhibition balance network dynamics arousal systems
axis_texts.problem_shape: many-to-one convergence; identify the invariant circuit signature
axis_texts.failure: molecular-target theories do not predict consciousness loss; correlates abound, mechanism absent

claims.title: Robust prior-free combinatorial auction design
claims.statement: Designing combinatorial auctions whose revenue and efficiency guarantees hold without distributional knowledge of bidder values, and remain computationally tractable with expressive bids, lacks a satisfactory general theory.

axis_texts.semantic: Get good auction guarantees without knowing bidder value distributions.
axis_texts.mechanism: prior-free mechanisms compete against benchmarks; combinatorial structure defeats tractability
axis_texts.math_structure: mechanism design incentive compatibility approximation algorithms worst-case analysis learning theory
axis_texts.problem_shape: unknown environment made harmless by design; expressiveness versus tractability tension
axis_texts.failure: distributional assumptions sneak back in via benchmarks; welfare-revenue tradeoffs unresolved

claims.title: Automated loop invariant inference at scale
claims.statement: Automatically synthesizing the inductive invariants needed to verify realistic loops remains fragile: template-based, constraint-based, and learning-based methods each fail on loops outside their assumed shape, and no method reliably finds non-obvious nonlinear invariants.

axis_texts.semantic: Find the right shape of loop invariants automatically instead of guessing templates.
axis_texts.mechanism: inductive assertions exist but their discovery resists systematic search
axis_texts.math_structure: fixed points inductive assertions constraint solving abstract interpretation
axis_texts.problem_shape: search space explosion; template selection as hidden bottleneck
axis_texts.failure: methods tuned to linear arithmetic fragment on nonlinear or disjunctive invariants
